title: Invariants
description: Load-bearing invariants for a codebase. Consumed by /triage, /invariants-review, /invariants-update, and other workflows. One file per repo, typically at proj/invariants.yaml or docs/invariants.yaml.

id.description: Kebab-case, unique within file. Referenced from code comments (// invariant lib-policy-free: ...) and from review tool output.

subsystems.description: Plain-English tags matching how a contributor would describe the area in an issue or PR. Use multiple tags generously (e.g. [sandbox, linux, landlock]) to improve matching. Avoid graphify community IDs — they shift between rebuilds.

statement.description: One sentence or short paragraph stating the invariant. Must be actionable — a rule a reviewer can check, not a vague principle. 'Handle errors well' is not actionable; 'Return Result; library code must not .unwrap()' is.

source.description: Doc reference or URL. Two accepted forms: (a) 'path/to/doc.md#anchor' — relative to repo root, anchor is the doc's heading slug; (b) 'https://...' — external URL (GitHub issue, RFC, CVE, upstream doc). Never leave empty; if an invariant has no written source, document it first, then cite that doc.

severity.description: high — breaking it creates a security hole, data-loss bug, or correctness regression. medium — violates API contract, testing discipline, or platform behaviour. low — style, ergonomics, or process.

added.description: Optional ISO date when this entry was added. Helpful for /invariants-update to detect entries that have never been reviewed.

last_reviewed.description: Optional ISO date of last explicit review. /invariants-update proposes updates for entries not reviewed in N months.

tags.description: Optional free-form tags beyond subsystems. Useful for cross-cutting concerns (security, performance, api-stability) that aren't subsystem identities.

related.description: Optional list of related invariant IDs. Used by /triage to surface a small cluster rather than a single rule where multiple apply together.
